sources.title: Gemini 4 Argon — Model Card
sources.evidence: Reopened October 27, 2026 and checked the complete current card. Its model-dependencies section explicitly states Argon is a new model, not a modification or fine-tune of a prior model. Sparse MoE Transformer architecture is described without expert dimensions, routing width, total, active or component counts. The comparison table contains benchmark results, not parameter sizes.

sources.title: Gemini 4 Argon | Gemini API
sources.evidence: The stable identifier is gemini-4-argon. Its specification lists text, image, video, audio and PDF inputs; text output; a unified 1,048,576-token input/output budget; thinking levels low, medium and high; and function calling. Reopened October 27 for the parameter re-audit; the exact stable-model specification table supplies no numerical total or active size.

sources.title: Gemini 4 Argon: Built to solve your hardest problems
sources.evidence: Dated October 13, 2026. Announces global availability to developers, enterprises and subscribers, including the API. This establishes the public release of the catalogued model. Reopened October 27 for the parameter re-audit; capability, pricing and token-limit figures do not disclose a model weight count.

sources.title: Gemini 4 Argon: our next era of frontier intelligence
sources.evidence: Dated September 30, 2026. Announces rollout to selected trusted cybersecurity defenders through Fairwind while saying developer, enterprise and consumer access will follow. This is earlier restricted access, not the public API release.

sources.title: Gemini API Additional Terms of Service
sources.evidence: The model card directs API users to these terms. They govern service access and prohibit extracting or replicating the underlying models, including weights; this supports proprietary licensing rather than an open-weight license.

sources.title: Gemini 4 Argon Safety & Security Report
sources.evidence: Fresh October 27 full-text review of the complete 217-page October safety report. Its parameter occurrences concern a synthetic-task difficulty variable, protection of weights against theft, and factual knowledge encoded in weights, not numerical model size. Section 4.3 covers unauthorized distillation defenses, not a count-bearing base relationship. No total, active, encoder or other component parameter count was found.

sources.title: Model cards
sources.evidence: Reopened the current first-party index October 27, 2026. Argon, updated October 13, remains the newest listed Gemini card; no later Gemini card or comparison disclosure is listed. Fresh exact-name/ID searches for total, active and component counts supplied no supported numerical disclosure.

sources.title: Gemini 2.5: Pushing the Frontier with Advanced Reasoning, Multimodality, Long Context, and Next Generation Agentic Capabilities
sources.evidence: Argon’s architecture citations link into this older report and its bibliography. It concerns Gemini 2.X and comparison models from older generations, not Argon; no sibling parameter or architecture details are transferred from it.

sources.title: Gemini 4 Argon | Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform
sources.evidence: The versions table explicitly labels gemini-4-argon GA with release date October 13, 2026. It also confirms the combined 1,048,576-token limit. Reopened October 27 for the parameter re-audit. The model specification and feature tables give context, capability, lifecycle and deployment details rather than learned-weight counts.

sources.title: Models.dev Gemini 4 Argon record
sources.evidence: Baseline catalog source, accessed as a lead. It is not used to independently verify public technical claims.

sources.title: Gemini 4 Argon Model Evaluation: Approach, Methodology and Results
sources.evidence: Fresh exact-model search located the original five-page evaluation appendix, read October 27. It specifies benchmark methods, thinking settings, trial budgets and comparison results, with no numerical total or activated-parameter count. The four base models in PostTrainBench are benchmark training targets, not identified bases of Argon.

sources.title: What’s new in Gemini 4 Argon
sources.evidence: Fresh October 27 review of the current exact-model migration guide, including the model table and API changes. It supplies token limits, thinking controls, pricing and serving behavior, not model-weight counts. Sampling controls and output-token budgets do not establish total or active size.

sources.title: Gemini 4 Argon Review: Benchmarks, Price, Size, and Comparisons
sources.evidence: Fresh exact-model numerical search surfaced a greater-than-6T lead. Opened October 27: the article attributes this to unspecified blogs and explicitly labels it unconfirmed speculation, with no linked evidence for the number. It is recorded as an unsupported search lead, not parameter evidence; its pre-public-release availability and architecture statements are stale.

name.note: Official card and exact stable API model page use this name.

developer.note: Google DeepMind developed the model; Google is the catalog developer grouping.

family.note: The card explicitly places Gemini 4 in the Gemini series.

release_date.note: Earliest verified public availability of this stable model. September 30 introduced restricted Fairwind access; October 13 opened general developer and consumer access.

open_weights.note: Distribution is through hosted Google products and APIs; weights are protected against unauthorized release and extraction.

license.note: Descriptive classification for model access under Google service terms; page-content and code-sample licenses do not license model weights.

parameters_b.note: Fresh October 27 exact-name/ID total-size, component and lineage searches, reopened original documentation and current comparison/report checks found no supported nominal total. The card explicitly excludes modification or fine-tuning of a prior model, so no count-bearing base is identified. The greater-than-6T lead is unconfirmed speculation without developer provenance. Null reflects absent numerical evidence, not an exact tensor-census requirement.

active_parameters_b.note: Fresh October 27 active/activated-count and component searches, complete safety-report review and exact-model comparison checks found no numerical active count. Sparse MoE structure is explicit, but expert dimensions and routing quantities are not supplied. Benchmark results, task-difficulty parameters, protected weights and API controls do not establish a per-token active size.

architecture.note: The exact-model Architecture section explicitly specifies a sparse mixture-of-experts Transformer with native multimodal inputs; moe is the existing catalog classification.

context_window.note: Unified input plus output limit, including thinking and function calls; this is not a separate 1,048,576-token input allowance plus an output allowance.

modalities.note: Exact API specification lists these inputs and text output; PDF is retained as the catalog input type.

reasoning.note: The model card identifies a reasoning model, and the API supports low, medium and high thinking levels.

tool_call.note: Function calling is explicitly supported for gemini-4-argon.

description.value: Google Gemini reasoning model with multimodal input, text output, function calling, and a unified 1,048,576-token input/output context window.
description.note: Replaces promotional wording with documented API capabilities and clarifies the combined context budget.

patch.description: Google Gemini reasoning model with multimodal input, text output, function calling, and a unified 1,048,576-token input/output context window.
patch.notes: Sparse MoE Transformer; Google identifies Argon as a new model, not a fine-tune of an earlier one. Total and active parameter counts are undisclosed. Context is a shared input/output budget of 1,048,576 tokens. September 30, 2026 was a restricted Fairwind rollout; public API availability began October 13, 2026.

summary: Fresh October 27 parameter re-audit retains explicit null total and active counts after exact-model/ID searches, original card/API/launch checks, complete safety-report review, the current card index and newly examined evaluation appendix and migration guide. No count-bearing base or component disclosure was found; an unsupported greater-than-6T search lead is not adopted. All unrelated field assessments and existing corrections are preserved.
